$comment: Global sourcing registry for independent contest catalog construction. Every contest in the catalog must trace to a sponsor on this list. Organizations are grouped by tier: work top-down. URLs marked verified:true were confirmed during research; the rest are the organization's known primary domain and should be confirmed on first use.
sourcing_rule: NEVER populate a contest record from an aggregator. Only from the sponsoring organization's own published rules. If the sponsor's page cannot be found, the record stays unverified and does not ship.

known_derived_sources.name: ARRL Contest Corral (monthly PDF)
known_derived_sources.reason: ARRL states the Corral is generated from data maintained on the WA7BNM Contest Calendar and extracted for QST. It is downstream of contestcalendar.com, not an independent compilation.

known_derived_sources.name: SM3CER Contest Service
known_derived_sources.reason: Third-party aggregator republishing sponsors' rules. Use it to FIND a sponsor's own site if needed, then source from the sponsor directly.

known_derived_sources.name: DXZone / hamradioworld / club news posts
known_derived_sources.reason: Downstream aggregators. Useful only for locating a sponsor's primary domain.

tier_4_specialty_clubs.notes: Weekend Sprintathon, SKCC Sprint, QSO Party, Sprint Europe. High-frequency recurring -- monthly rules.
CWT (weekly!), CW Open. Weekly contests need a distinct recurrence type -- see note below.

DONE. Happy New Year, QRP, Handtastenparty 80m + 40m, Deutscher Telegrafie Contest, QRP/QRP Party, Schlackertastenabend, VHF/UHF, YL-CW-Party, ZAP Merit. Per-contest rules pages state each recurrence in German; four also give a 'nächster Termin' used as the cross-check. 'Goldene Taste' is an AWARD, not a contest -- do not add it. ZAP Merit publishes no closing time and ships verified:false.

BLOCKED -- NOT AN AGGREGATOR PROBLEM, A SOURCE PROBLEM. qrparci.org/contests carries prose only; qrparci.org/qrp-event-calendar renders nothing without JavaScript and exposes no data endpoint; the WordPress page list contains exactly one 'contests' page and no per-contest rules pages. Rules appear to live in the members' magazine QRP Quarterly. qrpcontest.com is a third-party logging service, NOT the sponsor -- do not source from it. Next step: ask QRP ARCI directly, or find their rules in a QRP Quarterly issue they publish themselves.

DONE. All ten verified. Best-documented sponsor found so far: per-contest rules pages plus a calendar page that repeats every rule AND publishes projected dates for 2026-2035, used as the cross-check. NOTE: podxs070.com rejects some automated fetchers -- a normal browser user-agent works.

DONE. Rule 5.2.2 states all three recurrences in words; the schedule page gives the dates. CORRECTION: there are THREE QSO Parties, not four -- 'There are currently three QSO Parties held throughout the calendar year' (Winter Phone, Summer Phone, 10-10 Day Sprint). No Fall party.
DONE. HF RTTY, January Sprint, Sprint75, Sprint PSK63. Rules PDFs state the recurrence in words; each contest page lists six years of dates as the cross-check.

DONE. WW RTTY (third full weekend in August, three separate 8-hour periods) and New Year RTTY (January 1st, 0800-1100 UTC). Site uses frames -- go straight to /contest/wwrules.htm and /contest/nyrules.htm.

DONE but SUSPENDED. Eight sprints verified (second Saturday / third Sunday of Feb, May, Aug, Nov) and recorded with active_until:2025, because fistsna.org states 'Sprints will NOT continue in 2026'. fists.org is only a portal -- the sponsors are the regional chapters (fistsna.org Americas, fists.co.uk UK). FISTS Friday is explicitly 'not a contest'; the G3ZQS and Nancy Kott memorial events are operating activities, not contests.

DONE. NAQP CW/SSB/RTTY plus North American Sprint CW and RTTY. CORRECTION: NCJ no longer runs an SSB/Phone Sprint -- the 2026 rules document is titled '(CW/RTTY)' and the Sprint page has no SSB anything. The Sprint records use the `manual` rule type because NCJ publishes dates, not a recurrence rule. NCCC Sprint is NOT an NCJ contest -- see the separate NCCC entry.

DONE. NS (CW) 0230-0300Z, RTTY NS 0145-0215Z, FT4 NS 0100-0130Z -- all weekly, Friday UTC / Thursday evening NA, DST ignored. Rules at ncccsprint.com/{rules,rttyns,ft4ns}.html, NOT nccc.cc. Entrant eligibility is inferred from the absence of a clause and stays unverified.
DONE. Second Sunday Sprint -- monthly, second Sunday night LOCAL, 7-9 PM central. Local-time contest: the sponsor states outright that the UTC time moves with CST/CDT.

Spartan Sprint DONE -- first MONDAY of every month US local (Tuesday UTC), 2 hours, 'Does not shift for DST', so local-time. The working URL is ars-qrp.com, not arsqrp.blogspot.com. Flight of the Bumblebees still to do.

tier_4_specialty_clubs.org: Stew Perry / Boring Amateur Radio Club
tier_4_specialty_clubs.notes: Topband Challenge -- runs multiple times per year.

tier_5_qso_parties.notes: Roughly 45 US state QSO parties plus Canadian provincial parties. Each has its own sponsoring club and site. The State QSO Party Challenge (stateqsoparty.com) indexes them but is itself an aggregator -- use it only to locate sponsors, then source from each sponsor directly. Florida QSO Party is local priority for GCCC.

engine_gaps.detail: CWops CWT runs weekly; SKCC Sprint, ARS Spartan Sprint, 4SQRP Second Sunday Sprint and NCCC Sprint run monthly. The current engine produces at most one occurrence per contest per year.
engine_gaps.fix: Add rule types 'weekly' {weekday, times[]} and 'monthly_nth_weekday' {n, weekday}, and change expand() to return a LIST of occurrences rather than a single one. This materially increases catalog coverage -- these high-frequency contests are a large share of WA7BNM's ~500 entries.

engine_gaps.detail: ARRL 10 GHz has two rounds; Stew Perry runs three or four times a year; EME has multiple weekends.
engine_gaps.fix: Currently handled by separate records per leg, which works but duplicates metadata. Consider a 'legs' array on one record.

engine_gaps.detail: ARRL EME dates are set annually based on lunar conditions and have no fixed rule.
engine_gaps.fix: Add rule type 'manual' with an explicit date table, flagged in the UI as 'confirm with sponsor'.

engine_gaps.detail: ARRL 10 GHz runs on local time, not UTC. Flagged via local_time:true but not yet resolved per timezone.
engine_gaps.fix: Render local-time contests as a per-timezone offset at display time rather than storing a fixed UTC instant.

estimated_scope.note: Reaching WA7BNM's ~500 requires the long tail of small regional and weekly events, which is where the remaining effort compounds. 310 well-sourced contests covers essentially everything an active contester would ever enter.
